metric_rationale: This metric calculates the proportion of trials where the subject's choice aligns perfectly with the Take The Best (TTB) heuristic. Under TTB, subjects will consistently choose the option favored by the first discriminating feature, yielding a metric value close to 1.0 (subject to response noise). Under Tallying, subjects count the total number of winning features. The experimental design specifically pits TTB against Tallying on all trials: half the trials lead Tallying to choose the exact opposite of TTB (0% agreement), and the other half lead Tallying to a tie (50% agreement through guessing). Thus, data generated by the Tallying model will yield a metric value around 0.25, creating a massive and highly stable gap between the two theories.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Tallying heuristic's deterministic prediction on trials where Tallying does not result in a tie. Given the experimental design, Tallying and Take The Best (TTB) make diametrically opposite predictions on all non-tie trials. Therefore, data generated by the Tallying model will yield a metric value close to 1.0 (modulo noise), whereas data generated by the TTB model will yield a metric value close to 0.0. This ensures maximal separation between the two theories.

This metric isolates trials where the Weighted Additive (WADD) and Tallying heuristics make strictly opposing predictions (e.g., when one option wins on two high-validity cues, but the other wins on three low-validity cues). It calculates the proportion of choices on these critical trials that align with the WADD prediction. Data generated by WADD will score close to 1, while data generated by Tallying will score close to 0, providing a massive and reliable contrast between the two theories.

The experimental design includes key dissociation trials where Tallying and WADD make opposite predictions. Specifically, on trials where the sum of features differs between options, Tallying favors the option with the greater number of positive cues (higher sum), whereas WADD favors the option with fewer but much more valid cues (lower sum). This metric computes the proportion of choices that align with the Tallying heuristic on these diagnostic trials. Tallying will produce a high value (close to 1), while WADD will produce a low value (close to 0).
